Economic Community and Rural Development Directorate 
 
Tipperary County Council’s Economic, Community and Rural Development Directorate plays a vital role in fostering 
inclusive growth across the county. The council is committed to ensuring balanced economic and social development 
by focusing on various sectors like local enterprise, rural regeneration, tourism, community services, and sports 
infrastructure.

Local Community Safety 
Partnerships (LCSP) 
The LCSP regulations and guidelines were issued from the Department of Justice on 
the July 31st 2025. The next step is to commence the process of member nominations. 
There is a requirement for a maximum of 30 members representing local councillors 
(these nominations were approved at the October plenary meeting 2024) public 
agencies and community and voluntary groups. This is to allow for the broadest of 
representation across community safety sectoral interests, demographic and 
community interests and to achieve the best community safety outcomes for that area.

Work has commenced on a sports action plan for the county. A steering group of 
internal and external stakeholders has been established and a survey has been launched

Local Community Development Committee (LCDC) 
Tipperary LCDC held one online meeting and one hybrid meeting since the last update. Dr. Fran Igoe, 
Local Authority Waters Programme Office (LAWPRO) presented to the members at the July meeting on 
maximising LEADER funding for the benefit of biodiversity, water quality, climate resilience and local

Social Inclusion Community Activation Programme (SICAP) 
North Tipperary Development Company presented a reporting template to the LCDC at the June 
monthly meeting. The template captures where SICAP Goal 2 (supporting individuals) referrals come 
from. The Social Inclusion Sub-Group were presented with the  SICAP Mid Year Review from both 
North and South Tipperary Development Companies in July. Both Implementing Partners continue to 
deliver on their annual work programme.  
 
Tipperary LEADER programme  
A targeted call for LEADER grants is currently open for enterprises and social enterprises to carry out 
projects which will contribute to developing the county’s green economy and employment. The minimum 
and maximum grant available is €10,000 and €80,000 respectively. The closing date for expressions of 
interest to either South Tipperary Development Company or North Tipperary Development Company is 
08/09/2025.  
A “Greening your LEADER Project” information guide has been developed by the LCDC.  It will help 
groups and people applying for funding to consider the environment and climate action at all stages of 
their project.

Age Friendly 
Tipperary Age Friendly are delighted to partner with the National Understand Together Campaign and 
the National Tidy Towns to demonstrate the importance of connections, community participation, 
provision of sensory planting and dementia awareness.

Cultural Companions Tipperary 
Cultural Companions Tipperary has successfully launched it’s first group in Clonmel, with over 25 active 
members. Cultural companions connect older adults together through a shared interest in arts & culture. 
Older adults meet up socially and attend events together making new friendships, helping to combat 
social isolation. To date the group have attended events in the STAC Chapel during the Clonmel Junction 
Festival, Clonmel Busking Festival, and SETU Waterford. It is planned to expand the initative to Cahir 
and Cashel in the coming months.

allowing them to borrow the pieces for their game.

Power of Place & People in Tipperary 
 
The Power of Place & People in Tipperary is a new community mapping project in partnership with The 
Public Participation Network. The aim of the project is to record details of Tipperary’s many great 
groups, organisations and services. When all information is gathered the aim is to promote everything 
about the community groups and the great work they are doing.  
 
The project commenced in early June in the Carrick on Suir Municipal District and since then our it has 
progressed to Thurles Municipal District.   
 
To date we have met with approximately 90 community groups/organisations. We have been welcomed 
with great enthusiasm. The groups/organisations are delighted to showcase the work they are doing.  The 
survey provides valuable data for understanding the needs and priorities of each group and also 
recognises the wonderful work that is being carried out in our Communities.

The following is an update on football initiatives & development by the two FAI Development Officers

Club Development 
 
The FAI Club Mark is a series of accreditation awards for grassroots clubs based on best practice in the 
governance, management and administration of a club and is now mandatory for all clubs to hold at least 
the entry level award by December 31st, 2025.   
Borrisokane and Clodiagh rangers were presented with their club mark awards in June; Cloughjordan FC 
and Slievenamon Celtic/Kilsheelan United FC obtained the entry level award in July.  
All clubs across the county that do not hold this award are being engaged with and supported. All clubs 
have engaged and are now registered for the award.  Ongoing continuous support is being provided to 
clubs who are in the process including, Garda vetting, safeguarding training, policy development, and 
coaching supports.

REACH Roscrea  
The REACH project in Roscrea has been completed under budget and on time with a final project cost 
of €3,096,367.  The state of the art centre has secured two Anchor Tenants, Herdwatch a Global 
Technology Company working with the Agri Sector and Tipperary ETB providing upskilling and training 
opportunities through their numerous FET courses.   
The remaining space approximately 2,000 sq ft provides flexible workspace solutions for businesses, 
entrepreneurs, and remote workers, offering private offices, hot desks, fully equipped meeting spaces, 
video conferencing facilities and high-speed gigabit broadband to support productivity and collaboration. 
The REACH Centre will be officially opened by Minister Dara Calleary at 2pm on the Tuesday the 2nd of 
September.

Collection of Textiles 
Environment and Climate Action expanded its collection of textiles service c. 2020 to provide for 
the location of clothes/textile receptacles at various Bring Centres dispersed throughout the 
county. The purpose of the expanded service was to increase the recycling levels of textiles, by 
enabling householders to dispose of unwanted clothes in support of the circular economy. 
  
However, the operation of the service has given rise to a number of issues in recent months. The 
volatility of the international political situation has resulted in challenging market conditions which 
have made it more difficult for service providers to access traditional markets for this waste 
stream. This has affected the frequency of the collection of materials from the Council’s suite of 
clothes banks. A further issue is the financial implication presented by these challenging and 
changing market conditions, which are not within the control of the local authority. 
  
In addition, the nature and extent of use of the service by the public has given rise to localised 
matters of concern where, due to banks being full, service users deposit their items of clothing at 
or adjacent to the clothes banks, thus creating an environmental nuisance. 
  
Tipperary County Council is not unique in its experience of these issues. Having regard to same, 
the Council regrets that it will not be able to continue the operation of the service in its current 
form. With this in mind, a procurement exercise was recently commenced, which seeks the 
provision of a textile collection service at the Council’s suite of Civic Amenity Sites, which are 
located at Cashel, Clonmel, Nenagh, Roscrea and Tipperary (Donohill). It is envisaged that the

Affordable Housing 
 
The Affordable Sites in Boherlahan 
 
In the first round of sales, 1 of the 4 available sites was sold, while the remaining 3 did not progress 
despite all Expressions of Interest (EOI’s) being exhausted. 
 
To generate further interest the scheme was advertised in Q2 2025, with a closing date of 30th May 2025.  
Since then, deposits have been placed on all 3 of the remaining sites.  Although the level of interest was 
slightly lower than expected the outcome is considered positive.  
 
Key differences in the second round of advertising included 
 
• 
Increased promotion through social media by Corporate Services staff 
• 
Strong support from elected members in spreading awareness 
• 
Clearer messaging in advertisements, advising potential purchasers to engage with the planning 
section early regarding proposed house designs. 
 
 
Affordable Housing Clonmel  
 
Two potential schemes have been identified in Clonmel. A business case for the first has already been 
submitted to the Department while discussions with the Developer of the second scheme is ongoing. 
 
The Department have in the last number of weeks sought additional supporting information to 
demonstration the affordability gap in Clonmel.  The Housing Section is currently gathering this 
information for the Department.  
 
Affordable Housing Nenagh  
 
An EOI process for interested developers in Nenagh was advertised over an extended period but no 
responses were received.  However, with improvements in the wastewater capacity in Nenagh, it is 
anticipated that planning applications and interest from developers will increase.
